<b>Gromlings</b> are [[Enemies (Silksong)|enemies]] in <i>[[Hollow Knight: Silksong]]</i>. They are young [[Groms]] that ambush intruders within their domain and quickly retreat underground when attacked.<ref>Gromling [[Hunter's Journal (Silksong)|Hunter's Journal]] entry: <i>"Young masked worm that delights in ambushing intruders within its tunnels. A frustrating fiend. They flee beneath the bone whenever I try to strike them down."</i></ref>

== Behaviour and Tactics ==
Gromling spawn locations are typically divided into groups, with only one enemy per group ready to attack at any given time. When a Gromling is killed or burrows underground, there is a 3–6 second delay before it either prepares to attack again or the turn passes to a different location. Shifting dust particles on the ground indicate a potential spawn point, but not all locations display this visual effect, nor does it mean that the Gromling is ready to attack.

While burrowed, Gromlings face a specific direction that is predetermined for each location. They only attack if Hornet is in front of them, which frequently results in her being ambushed from behind. Playing the [[Needolin]] forces them to emerge, regardless of Hornet's position. Once Gromlings burst from the rock, they screech in warning before leaping toward Hornet. After that, they crawl forward for 1-1.5 seconds before burrowing back underground, retaining any damage they have taken.

Due to their speed, Gromlings can be difficult to defeat with the [[Needle]], so [[Tools]] and {{CrestSlot|Skill|s}} that deal high burst damage can be used instead.

== Location ==
Gromlings can be found throughout the [[Wormways]].

In [[Act 3]], the majority of them are mutated by [[Lifeblood|Plasmium]] into [[Plasmid]]s. Only a few remain in the northeastern section of the area.

On the maps below, Gromling spawn location groups are colour-coded and labelled with a letter. Within these groups, only one enemy can attack at a time. Regular markers indicate ungrouped Gromlings, which are always active.

However, with the exception of the Gromling in the southern Wormways, individual Gromlings have their own unique behaviours:

* The Gromling in [[Weavenest Karn]] has a 50% chance of not spawning at all when Hornet enters the room. If it does spawn, there is a 50% chance it disappears each time it is killed or burrows underground, returning only when Hornet re-enters the room.
* Two Gromlings near the pilgrim's corpse in the northeastern Wormways simultaneously ambush Hornet and then disappear, only respawning when she re-enters the room. Additionally, a nearby group of two spawn locations becomes active only after this ambush is triggered.
